title: Finite residue commutes with normalization of the completed coefficient presentation
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], A a commutative ring in the coefficient universe, I an ideal, and K an arbitrary unbounded derived module over adicLisseCompletedRing X I. Normalize K by SfbCompletionNormalization.object [lem-sfb-completion-normalization], and extend along the zeroth normalized projection to the constant ring A/I. This object is isomorphic to the exact derived transport of sfbResidueComplex X I K [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data] through the inverse AsSmall sheaf equivalence and inverse constant-scalar restriction [def-coef-constant-scalar-restriction]. No immersion or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Let c be SfbCompletionNormalization.coefficients and t the constant-ring comparison at A/I. The proved projection identity gives c.hom followed by the normalized projection p equal to the transported original projection followed by t.hom. Cancel c and t to obtain the inverse-oriented coefficient square. The sheafification compatibility equation shows that t preserves constant sections. Apply fixed_scalar_small_coordinates to identify H followed by the exact functor T of the statement with small-site module precomposition followed by restriction along t.inv.

Small-site precomposition commutes literally with scalar restriction. Restriction along a coefficient isomorphism is an equivalence, with inverse restriction along its inverse; the elementary cancellation isomorphisms are identity on sections. The inverse-oriented coefficient square and resCompIso therefore give a commuting square of exact restriction functors, with horizontal equivalences HB and HS. Derive the square using mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso. The completed scalar adjunction and the normalized scalar adjunction (the proved derived_scalar_adjunction specialization of sheafRingDerivedCoefficientAdjunction) identify its inverse mate as completedAdicDerivedChange followed by HS.mapDerivedCategory isomorphic to HB.mapDerivedCategory followed by ConstantCompletion.extend p. The inverse-mate theorem makes it invertible because HB and HS are equivalences.

Use the exact-derived factorization isomorphisms twice and Q.objObjPreimageIso to identify SfbCompletionNormalization.object X I K with HB.mapDerivedCategory.obj K. Similarly identify T.mapDerivedCategory.obj (Q.obj (sfbResidueComplex X I K)) with HS.mapDerivedCategory.obj ((completedAdicDerivedChange X pi).obj K). Keep the original smaller localization universe on fixed-scalar pro-etale sheaves, and the standard localizations on module sheaves. Apply extend p to the first isomorphism, compose the inverse mate at K, and compose the inverse of the second isomorphism. This is the required comparison for arbitrary unbounded K.
